title: goft configuration
description: A goft configuration: the settings of the service itself and the jobs it runs. A job file named by job_files holds a jobs list and nothing else. goft checks every file against this schema when it starts, then checks what a schema cannot: that directories exist, and the jobs against each other.

service.description: What belongs to the process rather than to any one job.

lock_dir.description: Holds a lock for each running job, so that the same job is never run by two processes at once. Defaults to goft\locks under ProgramData on Windows, and elsewhere to /tmp/goft-<uid>, private to the account goft runs as.

job_files.description: More jobs, from other files: each holds a jobs list and nothing else. A pattern may match nothing; a file named in full must exist. Relative names are resolved against the directory of this file.

jobs.description: The jobs. Every job is checked at startup, alone and against the others, and one that is wrong stops goft starting at all.

env.description: A reference to an environment variable, ${NAME}, replaced with its value when goft reads the file. goft checks the value once it is replaced.

duration.description: A length of time: a number with a unit, ns, us, ms, s, m or h, such as 30s, 5m or 1h30m. 0 needs no unit.

job.description: One transfer: which files, between where and where, in which direction, and what happens to them afterwards.

name.description: Identifies the job in every log record, on the command line and in its lock. Unique; names that differ only in case count as the same.

direction.description: send moves files from local to remote, recv from remote to local.

enabled.description: false leaves the job out of the service; --run-once can still run it.

local.description: The local side of the transfer: the source for send and the destination for recv.

path.description: The directory goft reads from or writes to. It must exist.

recursive.description: true also descends into subdirectories, recreating the tree on the receiving side.

include.description: Glob patterns matched against the file name: a file must match one of these.

exclude.description: Glob patterns matched against the file name: a file must match none of these. They also prune directories when recursive is set.

max_file_size_mb.description: Files larger than this are skipped. 0 means no limit.

poll_interval.description: The pause between cycles while running as a service.

stable_duration.description: How long a file's size and modification time must stay unchanged before it counts as finished being written.

workers.description: How many files are transferred at once, and so how many connections a cycle opens to each side.

verify.description: How a transferred file is checked: hash compares xxHash after reading the file back from the destination, length compares sizes only, none accepts anything that did not fail.

on_exists.description: What to do about a destination file that is already there: skip leaves it alone, overwrite replaces it unless verify shows the two are already identical.

post_action.description: What becomes of the source file once it has arrived: none leaves it, delete removes it, move relocates it under move_to (send only).

move_to.description: Where post_action: move puts the source file, keeping its relative path. It must not be inside local.path.

remove_empty_dirs.description: Removes a subdirectory of the sending side once the transfer has taken the last file out of it. Needs post_action delete or move.

retry.description: How a failed file is attempted again within the same cycle.

max_attempts.description: Counts the first try; 1 disables retrying.

interval.description: The wait before the first retry.

backoff.description: Multiplies the wait after each attempt; 1 keeps it constant.

remote.description: The other side of the transfer: a server and how to reach it, or with protocol local a second directory on this machine. Anything left out may be filled in from the Windows Credential Manager, ~/.ssh/config (sftp) or ~/.netrc (ftp); what is set here always wins.

protocol.description: ftp, sftp, smb, or local for a second directory on this machine.

host.description: The server. For sftp it may be a ~/.ssh/config Host alias.

port.description: Defaults to 21 for ftp, 22 for sftp and 445 for smb.

path.description: The directory on the server. For smb it is relative to share and must not repeat it; for local it is a directory on this machine.

user.description: The user to log in as.

password.description: The password to log in with. ${NAME} keeps it out of this file.

private_key.description: sftp: the key file, and the only key offered.

private_key_passphrase.description: sftp: unlocks private_key. Not needed when ssh-agent holds the key.

use_ssh_agent.description: sftp: false stops the ssh-agent being asked for keys.

ssh_agent.description: sftp: the agent to ask, a Unix socket or on Windows a named pipe. Left out, it is found as ssh finds it.

known_hosts.description: sftp: the known_hosts file that verifies the host key.

insecure_skip_host_key_check.description: sftp: true connects without verifying the host key.

ssh_config_file.description: sftp: read this file instead of the usual ssh_config search.

netrc_file.description: ftp: read this file instead of the usual netrc search.

use_credential_manager.description: Windows: false stops the Credential Manager being read.

credential_target.description: Windows: the Credential Manager entry to read instead of goft:<protocol>://<host>.

share.description: smb: the share to mount. Do not repeat it in path.

case_insensitive.description: Whether this side treats A.csv and a.csv as one name. Left out, goft decides: a directory on Windows or macOS and an SMB share do, an sftp or ftp server is taken not to.

connect_timeout.description: How long opening a connection may take, from asking ssh-agent for keys through the login to mounting the share.

io_timeout.description: How long an open connection may go without moving any data while something is waiting on it. It measures silence, not duration. 0 turns it off.

log.description: Where the log goes, how much is written, and how the file is split up over time.

path.description: The log file. Left out, the log goes to stdout, or to stderr when the human readable console has stdout.

level.description: Which records are written, and how much the console shows.

fields.description: The parameters each transferred file is recorded with. Left out, all of them but rate_mibs, which joins them at debug level; named, exactly those.

rotation.description: Splits the file by size, by day or by month.

max_size_mb.description: Starts a new file once the current one grows past this many megabytes, whatever the rotation. 0 means 100.

max_backups.description: How many old files are kept. 0 keeps them all.

max_age_days.description: How many days old files are kept. 0 keeps them however old.

compress.description: gzips the files that have been rotated away.
